title: Provisioning: emit structured stage events w/ correlation IDs (logs + metrics plumbing)
author: Caleb Johnson
body:
Motivation: The provision-to-ready automation sprint needs a reliable, queryable event stream for each pool provisioning run so we can (a) compute time-to-ready overall + per stage, (b) debug stuck runs without grepping unstructured logs, and (c) drive alerting with consistent error categorization. This PR introduces a small structured event model for provisioning stages (start/finish/failure) with correlation IDs, and plumbs those fields through logging + metrics-friendly emission points.

What’s in this PR: 1) Add a ProvisioningCorrelationID (run_id) that is generated at run trigger time and propagated through internal calls and queued work; 2) Introduce a canonical ProvisioningStageEvent type: stage (enum), transition (start|finish|failure), timestamps, attempt, pool_id, region, sku (optional), actor, and a normalized error block (error_code + error_class + message) for failures; 3) Emit events at the boundary of each stage transition (state machine) and at worker stage handlers, with a single helper to ensure consistent field names and avoid drift; 4) Log enrichment: all stage logs include run_id, pool_id, stage, attempt, and transition so we can slice across services; 5) Metrics plumbing: events are emitted in a form that can be consumed by the metrics pipeline (follow-up PR adds histograms/counters based on these events).

Event format (illustrative): {"event_type":"provisioning.stage","run_id":"prun_01H...","pool_id":"pool_9b7f...","stage":"IMAGING","transition":"failure","attempt":2,"ts":"2025-02-19T03:12:44Z","error_code":"IMAGE_PULL_TIMEOUT","error_class":"DEPENDENCY","message":"Timed out pulling golden image from mirror us-east-1"}.

Implementation notes: - run_id is a short, URL-safe identifier with a stable prefix (prun_) to make log searching easier; - we intentionally do NOT include customer_name in event payload to avoid accidental PII propagation and reduce cardinality risk; consumers should join via pool_id in the control plane; - stage is a closed enum aligned to the state machine: REQUESTED, PROVISIONING, IMAGING, BOOTSTRAPPING, VALIDATING, READY, FAILED; - transition events are emitted at the time we persist the state transition where possible to avoid “phantom success” on retries; - error_code is a constrained string set (consts) to make alert routing sane; free-form error messages are still logged but not intended for metric labels.

Testing: - unit tests for event serialization and required field validation; - integration-ish test around state transitions to ensure exactly one start + one terminal event per attempt (with retry) and that run_id propagation survives queue boundaries.

Rollout/compatibility: - this change is additive. No API changes exposed externally; - consumers are behind a feature flag in the metrics pipeline; - this PR only adds the event emission points + logging fields. Histogram/counter definitions are tracked in ENG-2749/PR-48239.

Follow-ups: - Wire the new events to the dashboard panels (observability-pack PR) and alert thresholds (SRE); - Expand error_code mapping as we discover new failure modes during pilot (keep set small).

Screenshots: N/A (server-side changes only).

Risk: Low-to-moderate. Touches provisioning execution path; mitigated by strict no-op behavior if event emitter fails (events are best-effort and should not block provisioning).
commits: controlplane/provisioning: add correlation ID generation and propagation helpers
provisioning: emit stage start/finish/failure events on transitions
logging: standardize keys for run_id/pool_id/stage/attempt across services
tests: state transition + retry semantics for event emission
conversation:
Allison Grant (review): Can we confirm the field names match our logging/metrics conventions? Specifically prefer run_id over correlation_id for consistency, and avoid putting error.message into metric labels. Caleb Johnson (author): Yep. I standardized on run_id everywhere and event emitter only exposes error_code + error_class as label candidates. error.message remains in logs only and is not exported as a label.

Aisha Bello (review): Stage enum includes READY/FAILED; are we going to double-count with state-machine transitions? We should be precise: stage is the logical stage, transition is start/finish/failure; terminal states should still be represented as VALIDATING finish -> READY start/finish? Caleb Johnson (author): Good call. I adjusted: stage enum is the active stage only (REQUESTED/PROVISIONING/IMAGING/BOOTSTRAPPING/VALIDATING). READY/FAILED are run_status fields in the terminal event payload (transition=finish/failure on VALIDATING) instead of stages. Updated tests accordingly.

Rafael Mendes (review): If event emission fails (e.g., downstream queue), does the provisioning run fail? I want a hard guarantee this cannot wedge the run. Caleb Johnson (author): Emitter is best-effort; failures are logged at warn with run_id + stage, but we do not return errors from the provisioning handler.

Vanessa Ortiz (review): Correlation ID propagation through queue payloads looks good. Please ensure run_id is generated once per run trigger and not regenerated on retry. Caleb Johnson (author): Done. run_id is persisted on the ProvisioningRun record and worker payload references that persisted ID; retries increment attempt but keep run_id stable.

Ethan Park (review): proto change: internal only? Any chance this leaks to customer-facing API surfaces? Caleb Johnson (author): Internal-only proto. No changes to public API. Confirmed by grep on gateway mappings.

Allison Grant (final): Approving; please file follow-up for documentation of error_code taxonomy once we have pilot data. Caleb Johnson (author): Filed follow-up under ENG-2748 subtask (comment) and added a short doc section in docs/internal/observability/provisioning_events.md.

Status: Approved by SRE + Platform + Infra; squashed and merged.
release_notes: Internal: Provisioning pipeline now emits structured stage events with stable run_id correlation for time-to-ready metrics and debugging. No customer-facing changes.
